claim.pdf_says: { 1 / 01 } constant-name-1 CONSTANT ... -- both level numbers in the leading brace are underlined (a short underline is printed under the "1" as well as under "01")
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown drops the underline from the level number 1. By §2014:5.2.1/5.2.2 an un-underlined word is optional, and a brace alternative that is optional can be implicitly selected (§2014:5.2.5.2), so the transcription reads as if the level number could be omitted entirely; the printed format requires 1 or 01 to be written.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered printed page 282 (PDF p306) at 300 dpi and cropped the leading brace of the 13.10.1 general format at 600 dpi: the brace stacks '1' over '01', and a short horizontal underline is clearly printed beneath the '1' (width of the single digit) as well as the longer underline beneath '01'. The markdown (page-306.md line 13) has '1' with no <u> markup while line 15 has '<u>01</u>'. The underline is the format's required-word marking, so dropping it from one brace alternative makes that alternative read as optional/implicitly selectable under the brace rule (§2014:5.2.5.2), whereas the printed format requires the level number 1 or 01 to be written. Not scaffolding, wrapping or formatting-only; the claim quotes both sources accurately.
